evidence.quote: In my view, we are not yet at that point. Reducing our policy rate too soon could result in requiring further future policy rate increases to return inflation to 2 percent in the longer run.
I remain willing to raise the federal funds rate at a future meeting should the incoming data indicate that progress on inflation has stalled or reversed.
the latest consumer price index (CPI) and producer price index (PPI) inflation data through January suggest slower progress in bringing inflation down toward our 2 percent target.
recent strong jobs reports—including upward revisions to employment growth—show a continued tight labor market.
I still see a number of upside inflation risks that affect my outlook.

parsed.rationale: The monetary policy section stresses slower disinflation, a tight labor market and several upside inflation risks, and it keeps open the option of a further hike while saying cuts are not yet appropriate. Most of the speech covers bank regulation, so policy relevance is medium.
